Torex Resources (TSX:TXR) Stock Stays Near Fair Value As Strong Q3 Cash Flow Lands
sum: Torex Resources has seen its share price move sharply in recent years, which puts a spotlight on a simple question for anyone looking at the stock today. Are the cash flows that the business can generate enough to support where the market is currently pricing it?
- Over the past 3 years, Torex Resources has delivered a very large total return. This puts more pressure on today's valuation to be grounded in the company's cash generation rather than sentiment.

- Recent updates highlighting strong free cash flow and lower all in sustaining costs suggest the operation may support more cash being available for reinvestment or future capital returns. This can affect what investors are willing to pay for those cash flows today.
- Prefer to judge Torex Resources on earnings? See why Torex Resources's 7.6x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The issue now is whether Torex Resources' current share price is justified by the intrinsic value implied by its cash flows using a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here projects what Torex Resources might deliver in future free cash flows and then discounts those back to today. On the latest twelve month view, the miner produced free cash flow of about $274.8 million, which gives the DCF a concrete starting point rather than a purely hypothetical curve.

Quebecor (TSX:QBR.A) Stock Still Looks Below Fair Value After 180% Run
sum: Quebecor has delivered a strong share price run in recent years, and that kind of climb naturally raises a simple question for you as an investor. Is the current price still aligned with the cash flows that the business is expected to generate, or has enthusiasm moved faster than the underlying money coming in?
- Quebecor has returned 179.7% over the past 5 years, which puts real pressure on the cash flow story to justify how far the valuation has already travelled.

- The recent 12.5% dividend increase, backed by strong free cash flow and a renewed buyback program, can support the idea that management is confident in the durability of the company's cash generation.
- If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why Quebecor's 16.8x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The issue now is whether Quebecor's current share price is supported by its cash flows when viewed through an intrinsic value lens built on those cash streams.
If you want to stress test the same cash flow question you are asking of Quebecor across a broader watchlist, take a look at 5 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here focuses on the cash Quebecor can return to shareholders over time. On the latest twelve month view, the group produced roughly CA$1.36b of free cash flow, and the projections behind this DCF assume those cash streams keep growing rather than shrinking, then cool into a steadier phase.

Investor AB stock heads into strategy update on November 4
sum: Investor AB will host a Capital Markets Update on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, placing its strategy and three business areas at the center of investor attention. The company announced the event in an Investor AB press release published at 08:15 CET.

The webcast is scheduled to begin at 13:00 CET and will focus on Investor's strategy and business areas. Chief Executive Officer Christian Cederholm will join senior representatives from human resources, finance, Listed Companies, Investments in EQT and Patricia Industries.

The program also includes the CEOs of Sarnova, BraunAbility, Laborie, Nova Biomedical and Mölnlycke. Their participation gives investors direct access to the operating companies within Patricia Industries and puts portfolio execution alongside the holding company's broader strategic priorities.

Investor says its portfolio is organized into Listed Companies, Patricia Industries and Investments in EQT. The group describes its investment model as substantial ownership and board participation aimed at building strong and sustainable companies and supporting them in becoming or remaining best in class.

The event may provide further detail on capital allocation, portfolio priorities and the role of the three business areas. Those details are not included in the morning announcement, so the key investor focus is the management presentation and the comments from the participating portfolio companies later on November 4.

INQ Group AB (publ) raises SEK 7 million under convertible loan facility from new US-based investment manager
sum: INQ Group AB (publ) ("INQ" or the "Company"), listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ticker: INQ), announces that it has raised SEK 7,000,000 of additional capital under its existing secured convertible loan facility from a US-based investment manager.
The new financing is being completed on the same principal terms as the Company's most recently announced tranche of the facility, including a conversion price of SEK 0.16 per share.

The additional capital follows the conversion of substantially all of the Company's earlier convertible debt under Tranches 1 through 5. Following those conversions, approximately USD 1.55 million of convertible principal remained outstanding. The SEK 7,000,000 financing announced today will be added to that outstanding balance.
The financing further strengthens INQ's working capital position as the Company continues the commercialisation and expansion of its consumer, enterprise and education businesses.

Under the terms of the new tranche, the investor is entitled to convert outstanding principal together with accrued and unpaid interest into newly issued ordinary shares in INQ at a conversion price of SEK 0.16 per share, subject to customary adjustments.

The new tranche will also be mandatorily converted at the same conversion price upon completion of a qualified equity financing of at least USD 3 million equivalent at a subscription price of at least SEK 0.22 per share.

In connection with the new tranche, the investor will receive warrants for no further consideration with a value equal to 20 per cent of the amount funded. The warrants will entitle the holder to subscribe for new ordinary shares in INQ at a subscription price of SEK 0.32 per share for a period of two years. The final number of warrants and underlying shares will be determined in accordance with the terms of the financing.

items.t: Tesco (LSE:TSCO) Stock May Be 25% Undervalued Despite €1.7b Asset Sale
sum: Tesco has delivered strong share price returns in recent years, which puts a sharper focus on whether the cash the business generates can support where the stock now trades. With investors also weighing fresh corporate moves, the question is how much of the supermarket group's future cash flows are effectively being priced in today.
- Over the past 5 years the stock has returned 140.9%, so a lot of investor capital now hinges on how reliably Tesco can turn its operations into cash over the coming years.

- The agreed €1.7b sale of its Czech and Slovak businesses, with most of the roughly €1.2b net proceeds earmarked for share buybacks, can reshape Tesco's future cash flow profile by concentrating on UK and Irish operations while reducing the share count.
- Prefer to judge Tesco on earnings? See what Tesco's 17.9x P/E says about the price.
For investors, the debate is whether Tesco's current share price is adequately supported by the value of the cash flows suggested by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of the business.
If you are weighing Tesco against other options that also screen on valuation and fundamentals, it can help to compare it with companies in the 13 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model values Tesco by adding up the cash the business is expected to generate for shareholders in the future and adjusting it back to today. Tesco is currently producing last twelve month free cash flow of about £2.7b, and the DCF framework here assumes this stays in positive territory and grows moderately over time rather than swinging sharply higher or lower.

Investor AB stock: Capital Markets Update set for November 4
sum: Investor AB's next major investor event is the Capital Markets Update scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, 2026, according to Vontobel Markets. The meeting gives investors a near-term opportunity to assess the holding company's portfolio priorities after its third-quarter update.

Investor's adjusted net asset value reached SEK 411 per share on September 30, 2026, up 4 percent during the third quarter and 17 percent since the start of the year. The figure exceeded the 11 percent total return delivered by the SIXRX index over the same nine-month period.

Patricia Industries was the strongest part of the portfolio in the quarter. Its private holdings generated a 15 percent total return, while adjusted EBITA increased 26 percent year over year. Aggregate sales at the private subsidiaries grew 12 percent, including 7 percent organic growth in constant currencies.

The November 4 update is expected to provide further strategic detail on Mölnlycke's planned separation into two businesses and on Patricia Industries' acquisition pipeline. The event may also help investors assess whether the recent recovery in Investor's EQT investments can continue after a difficult nine-month period.
